subject: Dedicated capacity ask: Horizon Medical sizing & prioritization
messages:
From: Andrew Patel <andrew.patel@horizonmedical.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: infra@horizonmedical.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU sizing request and Q on contention rules

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re finalizing our internal hardware plan and want to confirm Redwood can reserve a persistent pool for our production inference. Early ask: 6x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (24/7), plus a 2x burst lane for peak ingest that can be preemptible.

Two important questions for our procurement/legal teams before we sign:
- If capacity contention occurs, what rules do you apply to choose winners? We need to understand preemption, SLAs, and credits.
- Can you guarantee isolation for KV cache and model weights for HIPAA-controlled pipelines?

I’ve attached a quick throughput estimate and our expected request shape. We’d like a proposal by Tue 6/25 if possible to meet our board deadline.

Attachments: Horizon_Dedicated_Sizing_v1.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Andrew
VP Platform Engineering
Horizon Medical

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Andrew Patel <andrew.patel@horizonmedical.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU sizing request and Q on contention rules

Andrew — thanks for the note and the attachment, looks good. High-level response below and I’ve looped in Ben and Marissa (capacity + deals) to confirm feasibility and conflict windows.

Short answers up front:
- Prioritization logic: reserved capacity with an active committed contract (Reserved pool) is respected first. For burst lanes we use a tiered fallback: dedicated burst (contracted) > shared preemptible > queued best-effort. If two customers have committed reserved capacity for the same physical pool we escalate to triage and apply the deal-priority matrix (SLA tier, ARR, legal constraints).
- Isolation: we can guarantee KV cache separation and model weight isolation for your VPC/private deployment and provide audit logs. Will list required controls in the formal proposal.

Next steps: Ben — can you validate that 6x A100 steady + 2x burst is workable in our west-2 region for the 09/01 target starting date and advise if any other customers conflict? Marissa — please draft an initial commercial term (monthly reserved footprint + burst pricing) we can share with Andrew.

I’ll follow up with a short SOE and a proposed prioritization promise we can include in the SOW.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 24 Jun 2028 11:48:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated GPU sizing request and Q on contention rules

Laura / Marissa — reviewed their sizing sheet. 6x steady + 2x burst in us-west-2 is provisionable but we have a collision window the week of 08/28 with an existing Reserved negotiation for BrightBridge Health (deal currently at legal). BrightBridge holds a partial commitment for the same rack locality in our west-2 cluster.

Options I see:
1) We can carve physical segregation: place Horizon into an adjacent rack with equivalent A100-class hosts. This requires advance notice and a 30% uplift on monthly reserved pricing to reserve the physical tranche for their SLA.
2) Give Horizon logical reservation (soft-tenancy) and honor Reserved capacity in steady state, but use our prioritization matrix for burst contention (higher ARR + enterprise SLA wins). This is lower cost but offers less hard isolation.
3) If Horizon absolutely requires preemption guarantees for the burst lane, we must either 1) shift BrightBridge to another cluster (operationally costly) or 2) offer a time-phased start (Horizon begins 09/15) to avoid overlap.

We should prepare a concise exec escalation note for leadership if they push absolute exclusivity. Also: BrightBridge has a stronger ARR and earlier signature date in our pipeline — that factors into the matrix.

Attaching quick capacity map (internal).

Attachment stub: internal_capacity_map_west2.png

-Ben
Senior Capacity Planner

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — quick triage and recommended path forward.

Summary of constraints:
- Horizon requests: 6x steady A100 + 2x burst (preemptible) starting 09/01.
- BrightBridge: active Reserved negotiation that may touch the same rack locality starting 09/01.

Recommended approach (minimizes customer impact, keeps ops overhead low):
1) Offer Horizon a contract with logical Reserved capacity (guaranteed steady-state 6x) and an SLA-backed burst allocation with defined preemption behavior. For hard isolation of burst, offer an optional "Dedicated Tranche" add-on at +30% that reserves the physical hosts for both steady & burst.
2) For BrightBridge, ask legal to confirm earliest enforceable start date. If their signature comes in before Horizon signs, they keep the physical tranche and we will offer Horizon the Dedicated Tranche or a delayed start. If Horizon signs first, we favor Horizon for the tranche only if they commit to the Dedicated Tranche uplift.
3) Provide Horizon with audit-ready isolation documentation and a rebuttal schedule (48h response SLA from ops for any contested preemption event) to satisfy HIPAA concerns.

Operational actions:
- Ben: prepare two SOW variants (logical reserved + burst vs. dedicated tranche pricing) and mark the affected rack region in our scheduler so we can prevent accidental overcommit.
- Marissa: prepare commercial language and a limited T&Cs addendum that covers preemption credits (service credits for involuntary preemption beyond X% of burst windows).
- Laura: coordinate exec escalation if Horizon requests absolute physical exclusivity without uplift.

Andrew — we can get the two SOW variants to you by the end of day Thu 6/27. If you’re OK with the logical reserved + burst model initially, we can sign and then convert to the Dedicated Tranche later with a 30-day notice.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Capacity Strategy — Redwood Inference
